name: Typed Decision Contracts
problem: Agent loops route every discrete decision through a generative model call, paying full completion latency and token cost for what is a classification, and receiving an untyped string that may fail to parse, drift from schema, or hallucinate a category that does not exist.
context: Multi-agent orchestration, control planes and harnesses where a bounded set of decisions must be taken repeatedly against structured program state: which model to route to, whether a pending tool call is safe, how to triage an incoming request, whether a task is complete.
forces: Accuracy versus latency and cost per decision
Flexibility of free-form generation versus the determinism software needs
Expressiveness of natural language versus type safety at the integration boundary
Centralisation of intelligence in one large model versus specialisation of each step
mechanism: Model a decision as a typed question against a declared state, evaluated outside the token stream: enumerate the allowed answers in advance (choice, ordered score, or boolean), return a calibrated probability per answer plus a confidence score, and let deterministic code apply thresholds. The decision surface becomes a function signature instead of a prompt, so invalid answers are unrepresentable and low confidence is an explicit, handleable state rather than a silent guess.
implementation_shape: A pure decision seam behind an existing interface: input is a validated state record plus a question set with declared types; output is a typed decision record with probabilities and confidence. Callers branch on thresholds, never on parsed prose. The evaluator may be a classifier, a rules table, or a small model - the contract is what stays stable. Adding questions against the same state must not multiply round-trips.
benefits: Type errors and schema drift become impossible rather than improbable
Confidence is first-class, so the low-confidence path can escalate to a generative model or a human instead of failing silently
Decision latency drops from seconds to hundreds of milliseconds, which changes what can be automated per request
Cost per decision decouples from output length, removing the dominant term in agent-loop economics
Deterministic testing: the same state yields the same typed answer, so decisions become unit-testable
tradeoffs: Requires enumerating the decision space in advance; genuinely open-ended judgement still needs a generative model
Introduces a second model class and therefore a second failure surface and a second provider relationship
Calibration must be measured, not assumed; an uncalibrated probability is a confident guess
Question design becomes the new prompt engineering, with its own evaluation burden
risks: Treating a decision model as a general replacement for reasoning and silently losing capability
Vendor lock-in at a point in the architecture that was previously provider-agnostic
Threshold tuning without recorded eval numbers, producing confident wrong automation
Over-classification: forcing a rich judgement into a small answer set and discarding information the caller needed
anti_patterns: Prompting a model for JSON and wrapping the parse in try/catch as the error strategy
Adopting the model class before the decision inventory exists
adoption_conditions: A written inventory of decisions currently resolved by generation, each with its allowed answer set
Measured baseline: p95 latency, cost per decision and error rate of the current generative path
A calibration metric defined before adoption, not after
The evaluator reachable only through an existing seam; no new root dependency and no network requirement in L0 paths
An escalation path to a generative model or a human whenever confidence falls below threshold
evidence: SRC-0075: Vendor report of 70-500 ms end-to-end latency and $0.042 per MTok input with free output tokens for a discriminative decision model class, against 3-329 s and $0.20-$10 per MTok input for frontier generative models.
SRC-0076: Independent framework integration implementing model routing and pre-execution tool-call guardrails on top of typed decisions, reporting up to 200x faster and 400x cheaper classification.
SRC-0077: Tertiary corroboration of the discriminative, typed-output, calibrated-probability design and of the vendor's own disclosure that benchmark workflows were self-authored.
NOT LOCALLY VALIDATED: no measurement of this pattern exists inside EOS. Recorded as external evidence only.
organizations_using_it: Closed-source coding harnesses (pre-existing built-in action classifiers)
